title: Raynaud normalization over the absolute integral closure of a Dedekind domain
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $B\subseteq\Omega$ be the integral closure of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $A$ be a commutative finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] that is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $A_K=A\otimes_RK$ is geometrically normal: for every field extension $E/K$, every prime localization of $A_K\otimes_KE$ is an integrally closed domain. Set $A_B=A\otimes_RB$ and $D=A_K\otimes_K\Omega$, with the usual tensor-product ring structures [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The natural map $A_B\to D$ is injective. Let $C\subseteq D$ be the integral closure of $A_B$ in $D$. Then $C$ is a finite $A_B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], a flat finitely presented $B$-algebra, and a normal ring. The canonical map $C\otimes_B\Omega\to D$ is an isomorphism. For every homomorphism $B\to E$ to a field $E$ and every field extension $E\subseteq E^{\prime}$, the ring $C\otimes_BE^{\prime}$ is reduced, meaning it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. The zero algebra is allowed. Neither Noetherianity of $B$, semilocality or excellence of $R$, nor module-finiteness of $B/R$ is assumed.

source.place: Appendix II, Theorem 1, printed p.73 (PDF page 69, zero-based), affine form; separable means geometrically reduced fibres. C is the normalization because the generic fibre is geometrically normal. Primary scan read online https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf; local archive WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal], $B$ is a normal domain with fraction field $\Omega$. Flatness of $A$ tensors the injection $B\hookrightarrow\Omega$ over $R$ to an injection $A_B\hookrightarrow A\otimes_R\Omega=D$. Tensor associativity identifies these maps and identifies $(A_B)\otimes_B\Omega$ with $D$. Base-changing a finite polynomial presentation of $A$ gives one of $A_B$ over $B$. Flatness also base-changes directly: for an injection of $B$-modules, tensoring with $A_B$ is the same as tensoring the underlying $R$-modules with $A$. Thus $A_B$ is flat finitely presented over $B$.

source.place: Integral closure in algebraic extensions; explicit tensor and presentation calculations

proof.text: For each finite intermediate field $F/K$ in $\Omega$, let $R_F$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $F$. Every element of $B$ belongs to such a field by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension]; its monic equation is unchanged there. Hence $B=\bigcup_FR_F$. By [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres], each $R_F$ is a Dedekind domain. Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $B$, and put $\mathfrak p_F=\mathfrak p\cap R_F$. Inside $\Omega$ we have $B_{\mathfrak p}=\bigcup_F(R_F)_{\mathfrak p_F}$: each fraction has its numerator and denominator in a common finite field. Every ring in this union is a field if $\mathfrak p_F=0$, and otherwise a DVR by [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr], thus a valuation ring by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. For $0\ne x\in\Omega$, choose $F$ containing $x$; either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ is in $(R_F)_{\mathfrak p_F}$. This proves that $V=B_{\mathfrak p}$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $\Omega$.

The hypothesis makes $D$ normal and makes $D\otimes_\Omega L$ normal for every field extension $L/\Omega$. A nilpotent in any of these rings is zero: its germ in each prime localization is zero because that localization is a domain; if the element were nonzero its annihilator would be a proper ideal, contained in a maximal ideal where the germ is nonzero. Thus $D$ is geometrically reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $C\otimes_B V$ is precisely the integral closure of $A_B\otimes_B V$ in $D$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-reduced-fibre-normalization] over $V$ with fraction field $\Omega$, which is algebraically and hence separably closed. Its input algebra is flat finitely presented by the same tensor argument as Step 1. It gives $C_{\mathfrak p}$ finite over $(A_B)_{\mathfrak p}$, flat finitely presented over $V$, with generic fibre $D$ and reduced fibres over all algebraically closed fields. Here subscripts $\mathfrak p$ mean localization in the base $B$.

source.place: Appendix II, Theorem 1 to Theorem 1′, printed pp.73–74; valuation input implemented by Temkin Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 3–5

proof.text: Keep $\mathfrak p$ fixed. The small nonempty system $B_f$, indexed by $f\in B\setminus\mathfrak p$ and enlargement of the finite set of inverted elements, has colimit $V$: fractions and their equalities give its universal property. Products combine finitely many denominators. Apply [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent] to $C_{\mathfrak p}$ to obtain a finitely presented $B_f$-algebra $H$ with $H\otimes_{B_f}V\cong C_{\mathfrak p}$. The algebra $(A_B)_f$ is finitely presented by Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-category-fp-algebras], after enlarging the denominators the map $(A_B)_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ descends to $(A_B)_f\to H$, with exactly that base change. Every later occurrence of $H$ means this fixed model after base change.

source.place: Tags 00QO (finite-presentation algebra descent) and 05N9 (lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras), applied to principal localizations

proof.text: Enlarge $f\notin\mathfrak p$ so $(A_B)_f\to H$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-finite-ring-map]: $H$ is finite type over $B_f$, hence over $(A_B)_f$, and its limit map is finite by Step 3. Enlarge again so $H$ is flat over $B_f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map], whose finite-presentation hypothesis is the chosen presentation of $H$. The inverse system $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ has limit $\operatorname{Spec}V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. It consists of affine qcqs schemes with affine transitions. The affine map $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}B_f$ is of finite presentation, by its finite algebra presentation and the affine comparisons [lem-trf-affine-geometric-fibre-reduced-comparison]. Its limit has reduced geometric fibres by Step 3. Thus [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-fibres-limit-descent] allows a further enlargement making every geometric fibre reduced. Finiteness persists by tensoring a finite spanning list, and flatness and finite presentation persist by the injection and presentation arguments of Step 1.

The chosen comparison $H\otimes_{B_f}V\cong C_{\mathfrak p}$ gives, after tensoring with $\Omega$, a canonical identification $H\otimes_{B_f}\Omega\cong D$ under $(A_B)_f$. Flatness of $H$ over the domain $B_f$ makes $H\to H\otimes_{B_f}\Omega$ injective, by tensoring $B_f\hookrightarrow\Omega$. Hence view $H$ as a subring of $D$ containing $(A_B)_f$. Its finiteness over $(A_B)_f$ makes every element integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], and localization of integral closure [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] therefore gives $H\subseteq C_f$. The normality of $B$ in Step 1 implies that $\operatorname{Spec}B_f$ is normal: its local rings are the corresponding local rings of $B$. This base is integral and affine qcqs. Step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] verify every hypothesis of [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal] for $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}B_f$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp.20–21, and Theorem 3.5.5, limit argument; verification of the finite model hypotheses

proof.text: For $c\in C_f$, the equality $H\otimes_{B_f}\Omega=D$ writes $c=h/s$ with $h\in H$ and $0\ne s\in B_f$. The element $c$ satisfies a monic equation over $(A_B)_f\subseteq H$, so $H[c]$ is finite over $H$: powers below the monic degree span. The map $\operatorname{Spec}H[c]\to\operatorname{Spec}H$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. It is an isomorphism on the generic fibre and on the open $D(s)$ since $c=h/s$. On both schemes that open is schematically dense: multiplication by $s$ is injective on the rings and all their localizations, as they are subrings of the $\Omega$-algebra $D$ and $s$ is a unit there. This is a finite $\eta$-modification. The conclusion of [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal], whose hypotheses were verified in Step 6, makes it an isomorphism. Therefore $c\in H$. This proves $C_f=H$ on an actual principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, not merely after localization at $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2; apply eta-normality separately to each integral element of the fixed relative normalization

proof.text: As $\mathfrak p$ varies, Steps 4–7 give principal opens $D(f)$ covering $\operatorname{Spec}B$, on which $C_f$ is finite over $(A_B)_f$, flat finitely presented over $B_f$. A finite subcover exists since an affine spectrum is quasi-compact, as recorded in [lem-trf-affine-geometric-fibre-reduced-comparison]; equivalently these finitely many $f$ generate the unit ideal. The corresponding opens in $\operatorname{Spec}A_B$ form an fpqc covering, by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] and localization flatness [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] makes $C$ finite over $A_B$. The flat-localization criterion [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-flat-localization-span] makes $C$ flat over $B$. For finite presentation, [lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality] applied over the opens $D(f)$ makes $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ locally of finite presentation. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives the required finite polynomial presentation of the global $B$-algebra $C$.

source.place: Zariski locality of finite, flat and locally finitely presented morphisms; Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize

proof.text: To verify normality of the prescribed ring $C$, apply [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] to the finite-type $\Omega$-algebra $D$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is locally Noetherian; it is normal by hypothesis. The section-ring theorem [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] applied to the whole affine open writes $D$ as a finite product of integrally closed domains. Now [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product], with $A=A_B$ and ambient ring $D$, says precisely that each prime localization of its integral closure $C$ is an integrally closed domain. Thus $C$ is normal; the empty product covers $D=0$.

Since $A_B\subseteq C\subseteq D$ and $D=(B\setminus\{0\})^{-1}A_B$, localization gives $D\subseteq C\otimes_B\Omega\subseteq D$. The second inclusion is injective because $C$ is a subring of $D$: a fraction mapping to zero has zero numerator. Thus the specified canonical map $C\otimes_B\Omega\to D$ is an isomorphism. By Steps 5–8 every geometric fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is reduced, since it lies over a principal neighbourhood where $C_f=H$. For any $B\to E$, put $\mathfrak p=\ker(B\to E)$; the induced embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\hookrightarrow E$ identifies $C\otimes_BE'$ with $(C\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}E'$ for every extension $E'/E$. By [lem-trf-affine-geometric-fibre-reduced-comparison], the residue-field algebra is geometrically reduced, so this ring is reduced. All arguments allow zero algebras and empty fibres; none assumes $B$ Noetherian or $B/R$ finite.

The generic fibre and reduced fibres follow from the affine fibre comparison. Edge cases A=0, D=0 and empty fibres were checked.
